reviews.reason: The cross-page river/fire/inability-to-look clauses are recovered, but አፍላገ is plural, not singular. The source also explicitly names his throne.
reviews.suggested_text: And from beneath his throne rivers of burning fire came forth, and I could not look.[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace a: “The printed Geʿez unit begins on PDF76 and continues on PDF78. አፍላገ denotes plural rivers; the burning description belongs to fire. The printed Greek parallel also has plural rivers, ποταμοί. The inability to look is retained.”
reviews.suggested_source_text: Retain the supplied Geʿez transcription; correct the translation and the note’s singular/plural claim.

reviews.reason: The body can retain ‘whiter than snow,’ but its stated source rationale is inaccurate: the supplied and printed Geʿez contain starred ኵሉ, ‘all.’ Apparatus5 records its omission in l n. Omitting it therefore needs an explicit Geʿez variant choice, not merely a claim that Greek ‘all’ was not imported.
reviews.suggested_text: And the Great Glory sat upon it, and his garment gleamed brighter than the sun and was whiter than snow.[a]
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace a: “‘It’ refers to the throne. The printed Geʿez includes starred ኵሉ (‘all’) before snow; apparatus5 records l n omitting it. This rendering provisionally follows that omission. The Greek parallel independently reads ‘all snow’; its wording is not imported into the body.”
reviews.suggested_source_text: Keep the supplied printed Geʿez, including እም*ኵሉ፡ በረድ። Add to source.note: “Translation provisionally follows the omission of starred ኵሉ recorded for l n in apparatus5; the printed base text retains it.”

reviews.reason: The angel/flesh exclusions and provisional selected-Geʿez title are defensible. However, apparatus12 concerns the honor/glory construction corresponding to Greek21, not a straightforward substitution of Greek20’s ‘Great Glory’ title. The unresolved OCR-check language should also be replaced with the present scan-grounded assessment.
reviews.suggested_text: And no one among the angels could enter and see the face of the Honored and Praised One,[a] nor could anyone of flesh see him.
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace both notes with a, anchored immediately after the title: “‘Honored and Praised One’ provisionally renders the selected printed Geʿez title construction. Apparatus12 calls the wording probably corrupt and proposes a reading corresponding to Greek διὰ τὸ ἔντιμον καὶ ἔνδοξον, an honor/glory explanation rather than this personal title. The body retains the selected Geʿez construction without treating it as certain or substituting ‘Great Glory’ from verse20.”
reviews.suggested_source_text: Retain the supplied selected Geʿez, including its starred title crux; no reconstructed Geʿez replacement is certified.

reviews.reason: The fire, proximity exclusion, and myriads clauses are retained. The final rendering is explicitly provisional: note a preserves both visible daggered parts, explains their syntactic combination, and distinguishes the Greek word/deed clause. This is a disclosed editorial interpretation, not silent deletion or certification of an emendation.

The repeated holiness expression, approaching, nighttime non-departure, and non-withdrawal are represented. ‘Holiest of the holy ones’ is responsibly identified as an interpretation of the heightened expression, without importing the Greek angel designation or asserting a particular rank.

The disclosed Greek-supported ‘hear’ plus provisional Geʿez holy/word choice is permissible, but the quoted Greek is wrong: the scan has singular accusative τὸν λόγον, not plural genitive τῶν λόγων. Restore ‘here’ and the temporal force of ‘until this point.’ Disclose that apparatus28 specifically questions ‘holy’ as a corruption of ‘hear.’
reviews.suggested_text: Until then I lay prostrate on my face, trembling.[a] The Lord called to me with his own mouth and said, “Come here, Enoch, and hear my holy word.”[b]
reviews.footnote_changes: Replace a: “The printed Geʿez word after ‘on my face’ is daggered. Apparatus25 treats it as corrupt and prefers the Greek posture reading, βεβλημένος. ‘Prostrate’ is a Greek-supported editorial repair, not a separately certain translation of that Geʿez form.” Replace b: “The selected Geʿez provisionally gives ‘and to my holy word,’ with ‘holy’ daggered. Apparatus28 questions the holy reading as a corruption corresponding to Greek ἄκουσον (‘hear’). PDF79 prints καὶ τὸν λόγον μου ἄκουσον, ‘and hear my word,’ without ‘holy.’ The body deliberately combines Greek ‘hear’ with provisional Geʿez ‘holy’; neither source independently supplies this complete combined wording.”
reviews.suggested_source_text: Retain the supplied Geʿez. Replace additional_translation_input.text with “καὶ τὸν λόγον μου ἄκουσον”; replace its role with “Greek imperative support at the selected Geʿez holy/word crux; Greek posture support also used for the daggered face phrase.” Add the posture support βεβλημένος from PDF79 to the source note.

reviews.reason: The opening lacuna and bracketed Greek supplement are correctly distinguished. The final note understates apparatus30, which calls the Geʿez form untranslatable and proposes a corruption corresponding to Greek bowing. An explicitly Greek-supported final verb avoids implying a securely recoverable Geʿez ‘look’ reading.
reviews.suggested_text: And one of the holy ones came to me and raised me.[a] He lifted me up and brought me as far as the door; but I bowed my face downward.[b]
reviews.footnote_changes: Retain a. Replace b: “The final printed Geʿez verb is daggered. Apparatus30 calls it untranslatable and suggests a corruption corresponding to Greek ἔκυφον. The final clause provisionally follows the printed Greek ἐγὼ δὲ τὸ πρόσωπόν μου κάτω ἔκυφον, ‘but I bowed my face downward.’ This is an explicitly Greek-supported repair, not a certified reading of the difficult Geʿez verb.”
